items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: I started learning out of the Thompson method.

ctx.x: So by the time you were in like junior high school, had you decided on your career path so to speak?

Well we can start a little bit earlier than that. When we moved to Buffalo my father decided I was going to be a piano player. And I took piano lessons. And we lived in downtown Buffalo for a couple of years, and I started learning out of the Thompson method. And then in 1952 we moved to Cheektowaga, New York, which is a suburb of Buffalo, and every time we moved I’d have to change piano teachers, and that piano teacher would start me over with their method. So like I was becoming very disenchanted. You know like…

stuck with it because it sure was a lot easier to play an acoustic piano than it was to lug that stuff around. So anyway, that thing kind of fizzled out. Then I took up the trumpet. That lasted for a couple of years, right up here at Parker School, a couple of blocks away. And that was okay but that didn’t work out either. And in 1956 Tommy and Jimmy Dorsey, the Dorsey Brothers Orchestra, came to Cortland. You went by it on your way here, it’s a place called Skateland. It was a roller skating rink. Now it’s just…
